prerequisites: Fractions and reciprocals with explicit units.
explanation: A rate measures work per time; a duration measures time needed for the specified work. Convert units before comparing rates.

worked.action: A worker completes one job in 8 days at a constant rate.
worked.justification: Equal work is done each day under the stated assumption.

worked.action: Rate =1 job /8 days =1/8 job per day.
worked.justification: Rate divides work by time; duration divides time by work.

worked.action: If a machine instead completes 1/5 job per hour, one job needs 1 divided by 1/5 =5 hours.
worked.justification: The reciprocal converts rate back to time only when the whole job and units are consistent.

hint: Choose work units and label each rate with work/time before calculating.
shortcut: Use work = rate times active time; a convenient common work unit can avoid awkward fractions.
limitation: The rates must describe the same job, remain constant during each modelled interval, and not interfere.
